recent_posts.title: 2K lays off staff working on free-to-play shooter Project Ethos, while hinting at "new direction and focus"
recent_posts.summary: 2K has laid off an undisclosed number of staff at 31st Union, the studio developing free-to-play roguelike shooter Project Ethos. New studio head Ben Brinkman cited the need to work 'more quickly and nimbly' and align team size with the current development stage. The game is also undergoing a creative shift, moving away from its original Fortnite-like hero shooter aesthetic toward a more fantasy-oriented visual identity and a refined 'skill-based PVP roguelike' description. The project remains on Take-Two's upcoming titles list despite ongoing turbulence, including the earlier departure of founding studio head Michael Condrey.

recent_posts.title: PlateUp developer acquires stake in Yogscast Games to form indie publishing partnership
recent_posts.summary: Alastair Janse van Rensburg, solo developer of the hit indie game PlateUp, has acquired a 30% stake in Yogscast Games through his company It's Happening — an unusual reversal where a developer invests in a publisher rather than the other way around. Van Rensburg will act as a consultant helping Yogscast identify and shape promising indie titles. Yogscast MD Simon Byron discusses the challenges of the current game market, including the declining reliability of wishlist metrics, the growing importance of demos and playtests over traditional press coverage, and the difficulty of standing out in an increasingly crowded market. Both parties emphasize a developer-friendly, collaborative approach, with van Rensburg already consulting on two new signings.

recent_posts.title: Unity Q1 revenue rises 17%, posts $347m loss following IronSource closure
recent_posts.summary: Unity reported Q1 2026 revenue of $508 million, a 17% year-on-year increase, driven by 23% growth in Grow Solutions fueled by the Unity Ad Network and Unity Vector. However, the company posted a $347 million net loss, largely due to $279 million in impairment charges tied to the closure of the IronSource Ad Network in March 2026 and the divestiture of mobile publisher Supersonic. Create Solutions grew 4% on higher subscription income. Unity also recently launched a new AI tools suite for game creators in open beta for Unity 6 users.

recent_posts.title: CCP Games rebrands as Fenris Creations following sale from Pearl Abyss
recent_posts.summary: CCP Games, the studio behind Eve Online, has rebranded as Fenris Creations after being sold by Pearl Abyss back to its CEO Hilmar Veigar Pétursson for $120 million ($100M cash + $20M crypto). The company retains its leadership, studios in Iceland, London, and Shanghai, and all development plans with no layoffs. As part of the transition, Google has acquired a minority stake and formed a research partnership with Google DeepMind, which will use an offline version of Eve Online to test AI models focused on long-horizon planning, memory, and continual learning. Pearl Abyss originally acquired CCP Games in 2018 for $225 million plus performance payouts.

recent_posts.title: Unity launches suite of AI tools to help creators accelerate game development
recent_posts.summary: Unity has launched Unity AI Beta, an open beta suite of AI tools available to all Unity 6 and above developers. The centerpiece is the Agentic Assistant, which helps developers navigate their projects and use Unity tools more effectively. Additional features include a 'Plan' mode for implementation design, 'Skills' for expert guidance in areas like UI and scene setup, instant rollback, and placeholder asset generation (materials, sounds, cubemaps, 2D/3D assets). Developers can connect external AI tools and LLMs via an AI gateway or Unity's MCP server. Pro, Enterprise, and Industry subscribers get the features automatically, while Personal Edition users can start a 14-day free trial with 1,000 credits, then subscribe for $10/month.

recent_posts.title: Founders of Gearbox Quebec announce new studio to "create original, premium games on our own terms"
recent_posts.summary: Former Gearbox Quebec founders Sébastien Caisse and Pierre-André Déry, along with ex-Borderlands Creative Director Maxime Babin and other AAA veterans, have announced Ricochet Games, a new Canadian studio. The team is self-funded and deliberately small, aiming to avoid the pitfalls seen in other veteran-led studios that scaled too quickly before proving their concept. Their first project is a premium, buy-to-play co-op action-adventure game for PC and console, explicitly rejecting live-service and GaaS models. The studio draws inspiration from Arrowhead, Remedy, and Sabotage, and cites creative references including Studio Ghibli and FromSoftware.

recent_posts.title: Valve commits to restocking its Steam Controller after it "ran out faster than we anticipated" | News-in-brief
recent_posts.summary: Valve has committed to restocking its Steam Controller after supplies ran out faster than expected, expressing regret that not all interested customers could obtain one. Separately, Supercell is acquiring Metacore, the studio behind Merge Mansion, a mobile merge-puzzle game that has been downloaded over 60 million times and generated around $700 million in revenue since its 2020 launch.

recent_posts.title: EA closes FY26 with "record" performance thanks to Battlefield 6 and Apex Legends
recent_posts.summary: Electronic Arts reported preliminary Q4 and full-year FY26 financial results, claiming a 'record' fiscal year. Q4 net revenue reached $2.1 billion (up 12% YoY) and net income hit $461 million (up 81.5% YoY). For the full year, net revenue was $7.53 billion and net bookings $8.03 billion (up 9% YoY), though annual net income fell 20.9%. Key drivers included Battlefield 6 setting franchise fiscal year records, Apex Legends posting its strongest Q4 net bookings with double-digit YoY growth, and Global Football net bookings growing mid-single-digits. The results come amid EA's pending $55 billion acquisition, expected to close in Q1 FY2027, after which Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund would own over 93.4% of the company.

recent_posts.title: Gamescom Latam attendance up by 17.5% in 2026
recent_posts.summary: Gamescom Latam 2026 drew 154,000 visitors, a 17.5% increase over 2025's 130,000 attendees. The São Paulo event featured 400+ games, 175 exhibitors from 23 countries, and generated an estimated $180 million in new business — a 46% rise in B2B meetings year-over-year. Executives from Abragames and Brasil Games highlight Brazil's growing games industry of 13,000+ professionals, its reputation for contract/outsourcing work, and increasing recognition for original IP. Key challenges include limited public funding, though lobbying efforts for tax incentives are underway.

recent_posts.title: Xbox announces leadership changes as it stops development of Gaming Copilot for console
recent_posts.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced significant leadership changes, including the cancellation of Gaming Copilot for consoles and the phasing out of the feature on mobile. The move comes just months after Xbox announced Copilot would arrive on current-gen consoles in 2026. Several new executives from Microsoft's CoreAI division are joining Xbox, while existing leaders are being reassigned. The restructuring aims to help Xbox move faster, deepen community connections, and address friction for players and developers. Xbox also plans to expand into China and emerging markets, strengthen Game Pass, and focus on growing daily active users despite a 33% drop in hardware revenue in Q3.

top_posts.title: Assassin's Creed Shadows' success shows that the threat of negative campaigns is overblown | Opinion
top_posts.summary: Assassin's Creed Shadows has performed well in sales despite intense online backlash and controversy over its protagonists, proving that such campaigns have limited impact on consumer behavior. This success highlights the resilience of the Assassin's Creed franchise and suggests that maintaining the quality of the game is more crucial than succumbing to bad-faith criticisms.

top_posts.title: Stop Killing Games EU petition hits 1.3m verified signatures
top_posts.summary: The Stop Killing Games EU petition has reached 1.3 million verified signatures out of 1.5 million total, surpassing the 1 million threshold needed for European Commission discussion. The campaign, which started after Ubisoft shut down The Crew in 2024, aims to prevent game publishers from permanently disabling games when online services end. Germany and France led contributions with 233,180 and 145,239 signatures respectively. The petition achieved a low 10% rejection rate, placing it among the most successful European Citizens Initiative campaigns. Industry trade body Video Games Europe and the UK government have responded, arguing that maintaining older game servers may not be commercially viable and that no law currently requires indefinite support.

top_posts.title: "It needs to cooperate fairly, and it's clearly not." Why Valve is facing a £656m day in the UK courts
top_posts.summary: Digital safety campaigner Vicki Shotbolt is leading a UK class action lawsuit against Valve, seeking up to £656 million in damages on behalf of consumers. The case, brought by law firm Milberg, centers on two key claims: that Valve's 30% revenue share on Steam constitutes excessive commission that inflates game prices for consumers, and that Valve's price parity requirement prevents developers from selling games cheaper on competing storefronts. A UK court recently ruled the case must proceed to trial despite Valve's objections. Shotbolt acknowledges there's no guarantee developers would pass savings on to consumers if Valve reduced its cut, but argues the price parity clause is the critical mechanism that locks in high prices across the market.

top_posts.title: Match-3 game ads accused of harmful stereotypes
top_posts.summary: Mobile game developers Microfun, Nanobit, and Magic Tavern have faced criticism for advertisements that reportedly reinforce harmful stereotypes and gender-based violence. While Microfun has pulled the contentious ads, the others remain online. The Advertising Standards Authority is aware of these campaigns, which have been accused of promoting misogynistic tropes to boost downloads of their match-3 puzzle games. The recent backlash connects to wider issues around the portrayal of women in media and advertising ethics.

top_posts.title: Mewgenics tops 1 million copies sold in just one week | News-in-brief
top_posts.summary: Roguelike Mewgenics sold over 1 million copies in its first week, reaching a concurrent peak of 115,428 players on Steam during its debut weekend. Separately, Brazilian indie studio Devcats has launched a publishing arm to support cozy and wholesome indie games, with its first published title being Feline Forensics and the Meowseum Mystery. Devcats plans to offer marketing, localization, music, and game direction support to indie developers, while contributing a portion of profits to animal welfare causes.
